title: Watching Trade from Space: Measuring Maritime Trade Using Satellite Imagery
abstract: arXiv:2604.15444v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: This paper combines synthetic aperture radar imagery, nighttime lights, and port characteristics to measure port-level maritime trade using only publicly available data. We evaluate the framework at ports the model has never observed, training on United States ports and testing on European ports and then reversing the exercise, and find that the mapping transfers in both directions. Applying the framework to Russian ports after the 2022 sanctions, we find reallocation, with the Far East the only basin rising faster than the movement common to all Russian ports. The approach complements methods based on the Automatic Identification System: where transponders broadcast, AIS-based estimates track official statistics closely, and after the sanctions the radar keeps recording activity at western Russian ports that disappears from the AIS record, which is where dark shipping concentrates.

translated_title: 从太空观察贸易：利用卫星图像测量海运贸易
translated_abstract: 本文结合合成孔径雷达图像、夜间灯光和港口特征，仅使用公开可得的数据来测量港口层面的海运贸易。我们在模型从未见过的港口上评估该框架——先在美国港口训练、在欧洲港口测试，然后将训练和测试顺序颠倒——发现这种映射关系在两个方向上均能成功迁移。将该框架应用于2022年制裁后的俄罗斯港口，我们发现贸易发生了重新配置，其中远东是唯一一个增速快于所有俄罗斯港口共同变动趋势的海域。该方法是对基于自动识别系统（AIS）的方法的补充：在应答器正常广播的地方，基于AIS的估计与官方统计数据高度吻合；而在制裁之后，雷达持续记录到俄罗斯西部港口的活动，这些活动已从AIS记录中消失，而这正是“黑暗航运”集中的地方。
tldr: 本文提出一种仅利用公开卫星数据（合成孔径雷达与夜间灯光）测量港口海运贸易的框架，证明该模型可跨国迁移，并揭示了2022年制裁后俄罗斯贸易向远东重新配置以及从AIS记录中消失的“黑暗航运”活动。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a framework to measure port-level maritime trade using only publicly available satellite data (SAR imagery and nighttime lights), demonstrates that the model transfers across countries, and reveals post-2022-sanctions trade reallocation toward Russia's Far East and dark shipping activity that disappears from AIS records.
